wu: Warm-up: 'Service Match' — students stand in two lines; teacher holds flashcards of city services (e.g., police, hospital, taxi); each student says a service and the partner responds with the number; teacher models first: 'Police?' '190!'
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Service Charades' — students mime a service (e.g., fixing a pipe) and partners guess the word
Alternative 2: 'Service Bingo' — teacher calls out services, students cross them off their bingo cards
pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of a phone and a service (e.g., hospital); model 'Could I speak to a doctor, please?'; drill the phrase with rising intonation; check understanding by asking 'What do we say to be polite?' and 'What number do we call for the hospital?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a real phone prop; dial a fake number and model the request
Alternative 2: Show a short video clip of someone making a polite service call
prac: Guided practice: 'Service Request Cards' — students pick cards with service scenarios (e.g., 'My taxi is late'); in pairs, they practice 'Could I...?' requests; teacher circulates and corrects pronunciation
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Polite Request Drill' — students repeat after teacher with different services
Alternative 2: 'Matching Game' — match requests to responses (e.g., 'Could I get a taxi?' to 'Yes, of course')
ls: Listening slot: Play a KET-style phone dialogue between a caller and a service; students listen and circle the correct service (police/hospital/taxi) on their worksheet; check answers as a class
re: Reactivation game: 'Number Relay' — students line up; teacher calls out a service (e.g., 'fire'); first student shouts the number (e.g., '150') and runs to the back of the line
prod: Production task: 'Back-to-Back Roleplay' — students sit back-to-back with a partner; one is a caller, the other a service worker; they use 'Could I...?' to make requests and respond; swap roles after 3 minutes
rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read short phone scripts and match requests to responses; then write their own polite request for a service (e.g., 'Could I book a table for two, please?')
st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Sing 'The Wheels on the Bus' with service-themed verses (e.g., 'The phone on the bus goes ring, ring, ring'); Close with 'Today we learned to make polite phone calls. Thank you, class!'
g: Students mime a service (e.g., plumber) and partners guess
Teacher calls out service numbers, students cross them off
Students repeat 'Could I...?' with rising intonation
Teams race to match services to numbers
Students roleplay phone calls with backs to each other
diff: Fast finishers: Write a dialogue for a tricky call (e.g., 'My electricity is out')
Support: Use sentence starters like 'Could I...?' on a worksheet
hw: Option 1: Write 3 polite requests for different services
Option 2: Record a phone call with a family member
Option 3: Draw a picture of a service and write the number
tip: Emphasize rising intonation in 'Could I...?' to sound polite; connect to local services in Oujda (e.g., police number) for relevance.
